summary_text: The department significantly exceeded its operating profit budget by $524,692, driven by a strong December sales surge from the postponed November product launch and robust year-end gifting demand. While COGS rose in line with higher sales, cost efficiencies in freight, marketing, and administrative expenses contributed to the favorable variance. Overall, the company demonstrated strong operational performance and effective cost management during the year-end period.

The Beauty (BT) department exceeded its operating profit budget by $358,122 (163.5%). This strong performance was driven by higher-than-expected December revenue due to the postponed November product launch, which shifted year-end demand into the month. Additionally, cost efficiencies in freight, marketing, and personnel expenses further contributed to the favorable variance.

The Health & Wellness department exceeded its operating profit budget by $105,947 (72.1%), driven by higher-than-expected revenue and disciplined cost management. Revenue outperformed due to strong organic demand, while expenses remained below budget across personnel, freight, and marketing categories, reflecting operational efficiencies and strategic consolidation of activities. This performance underscores the department’s ability to capitalize on favorable market conditions while maintaining cost control.

The Household Products department exceeded its operating profit budget by $29,321 (47.1%), driven by higher-than-expected revenue and lower COGS. Strong year-end promotional performance led to increased sales incentive payouts, which were partially offset by disciplined cost control across administrative, freight, and marketing expenses. Overall, the department demonstrated solid financial performance, leveraging operational efficiencies and favorable market conditions.

The Food & Beverage department significantly exceeded its operating profit budget by $31,302, driven by strong year-end snack and beverage gifting demand that boosted revenue far above expectations. While COGS and marketing expenses increased in line with higher sales, personnel expenses remained tightly controlled, contributing to the favorable variance. The overall performance reflects effective cost management and robust demand during the peak holiday season.
